purpose: Exam-type-aware Semester 2 test bank for Diploma Computer Engineering

mcq.Options: 120 JSON strings flattened in A-D groups

testIdRule: TestId = decimal SubjectId concatenated with the per-subject test occurrence. For isDepartmentalSubject=false: 1-12 Mid 1, 13-24 Mid 2, 25-36 ESE. For true: 1-12 Mid 1, 13-24 Mid 2.
notes: Mid 1 is scoped to the first half of ordered syllabus units as recorded in test_index/subject_index.
TestsData does not contain subject, exam type, difficulty or marks columns; use test_index.
Theory rows use Options=[] and Answers contains matching model answers. The consumer must support theory rows explicitly.
Generated source items are syllabus-topic-derived drafting items; content review is required before production.
Variants differ by sampled questions/options within each difficulty; some source concepts recur across variants.

subjects.name: Applied Physics
subjects.objective: To prepare the students to have a basic knowledge of fundamental quantities, their units and measurement. To study various cases under laws of motion. To have knowledge of various properties of maters also to have knowledge of fundamentals of electricity and magnetism and to have knowledge about Light and Sound Waves.
course_outcomes: To measure dimensions of various materials and compare units.
To understand and relate phenomena with the help of laws of motion.
To identify various states of materials and their relevance.
To understand the concept of Electricity and Magnetism and its application in daily life.
To get Knowledge about Light and Sound Waves and their applications.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Units, Dimensions and Measurements
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition of unit, Fundamental and Derived units, systems of units- CGS, MKS and SI, introduction to accuracy, precision and errors, types of errors, error analysis, Numerical on Error

allSyllabusUnits.title: Laws of Motion
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Inertia, Newton's first law of motion, momentum, Newton’s second law of motion, conservation of momentum, Newton's third law of motion, Numerical on above topics

allSyllabusUnits.title: Properties of Matter
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Stress & strain along with their types, Hooke's law and modulus of elasticity-Young, bulk and modulus of rigidity, Viscosity, newton's law of viscosity, types of flows, Reynold's number, surface tension and capillary action

allSyllabusUnits.title: Electro-Magnetism
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Current electricity: current, EMF and Ohm's law, resistance, series and parallel, Numerical on above topics, Magnetism: Magnetic field and properties, electro-magnetic induction-self-inductance and mutual inductance, faraday’s law, applications-transformer

allSyllabusUnits.title: Waves: Light & Sound
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Light: Properties, Reflection, Refraction, Snell’s law, Dispersion of light, Sound: Characteristics – (Amplitude, Wavelength, Crest, Trough, Frequency, Time Period), Definition of Resonance with Examples, Formula for Velocity of Sound and factors affecting it, Ultrasonic Sound Waves – Uses, properties, Applications, Radioactive rays - Properties and uses of Alpha, Beta and Gamma particles. Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Units, Dimensions and Measurements; Laws of Motion; Properties of Matter.

subjects.name: Basic Electronics
subjects.objective: This subject provides an opportunity for the students to get familiarized with all basic electronics components and study the characteristics of diode, transistors etc. Also student will get the ability to do simulation of corresponding circuits. The lab is designed for second semester students.
course_outcomes: Develop the conceptual knowledge about the semiconductor and learn fundaments of terminal characteristics of PN junction diode and design
Identify limitation of diode and learning fundaments of transistor structure, types and behavioral characteristics and comparison of various transistor configurations.
Exploring the DC load line, biasing methods, and applications of transistor.
To build basic circuits using liner IC s.
To troubleshoot electronic circuits.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Diode characteristics and its applications
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Types of semiconductors., P-N junction diode formation and characteristics., Applications - Diode as rectifier, half wave, full wave and bridge rectifier, clipping and clamping circuit., Need of filters., Need of filters., Zener diode & it's application, Photo diode, LDR, Photovoltaic Cell, Light Emitting Diode, Varactor Diode, Digital display

allSyllabusUnits.title: Transistor characteristics and applications
allSyllabusUnits.topics: PNP and NPN transistors, conduction through transistor leakage current, relationship between a and ß., Transistor configuration & characteristics for CB, CE, CC. Load line and biasing methods of transistor., Common emitter amplifier. Common collector amplifier. Multistage amplifier, Construction of JFET, Characteristics of JFET

allSyllabusUnits.title: Integrated circuits, Cables and Connectors
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Need of IC¶s. Block diagram of operation amplifier. Characteristics and specification of op amp , Applications of op amp, Block diagram of IC555, Working of IC555, Applications of IC 555, Mono stable, bi stable, astable Multivibrator and timer circuit, Cables: coaxial cable, twisted pair cable and fiber optic cable, Connectors: coaxial cable connectors, RJ-45, RS-232, HDMI connectors. Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Diode characteristics and its applications; Transistor characteristics and applications.

subjects.name: Computer Network Skills
subjects.objective: This subject will help to understand fundamental concepts of computer networking. Make students knowledgeable about basic taxonomy and terminology of the computer networking area. Offers advanced networking concepts, preparing the student for entry Advanced courses in computer networking
course_outcomes: Apply the fundamental concepts of data communication in practical networking scenarios
Identify and select appropriate types of networking cables for specific communication needs
Classify networks based on range, topology, and architecture to suit different use cases
Demonstrate the use of various networking devices in the setup and functioning of a network

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Overview of computer network, usage of computer network, line configuration- point-to-point, multi point, types of server, Data flow-simplex, Half duplex, Full Duplex

allSyllabusUnits.title: Cabling
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction to network cabling, Unshielded Twisted Pair (UTP) Cable, Twisted Pair (STP) Cable, Coaxial Cable, Fiber Optic Cable

allSyllabusUnits.title: Types of network & Topology
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Importance of computer network, Local Area Network (LAN), virtual LAN (VLAN), Controller Area Network (CAN), Metropolitan Area Network (MAN), Wide Area Network(WAN), Internet and Intranet, Extranet, , Topology - Star, Bus, Mess, Ring, Hybrid,, Pros and Cons of each topology

allSyllabusUnits.title: Transmission media
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Types of transmission media, Guided transmission media-twisted pair, coaxial cable, optical fiber, magnetic media, Unguided transmission media-light transmission, microwave transmission, radio transmission, infrared transmission

allSyllabusUnits.title: Network devices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Working of Networking Components – Hubs , Bridges, Switches (Manageable and Non-Manageable), Switching and Forwarding Routers, Gateways, Access Point, Modem, Wi-fi-Router Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Introduction; Cabling; Types of network & Topology.

subjects.name: Computer Programming
subjects.objective: This Course will help to develop programming skills in the students, using a structured programming language ‘C’'. Students will learn stepped procedure of any program development process using flowchart and algorithms. The programming skill will help to work with advance level programming languages which in turn will be helping in developing programs for the scientific, research and business purposes.
course_outcomes: Apply the fundamental concepts of C language to solve basic programming problems
Construct logical solutions using flowcharts and algorithms for given problem scenarios
Implement appropriate C programming syntax to develop functional code
Use suitable control structures, loops to address specific real-time application requirements
Translate real-world problems into algorithms and develop corresponding C programs
Apply basic programming principles to design structured and modular C programs

allSyllabusUnits.title: Flowchart & Algorithm
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Problem solving using flowchart and algorithm, Flowchart- Importance of flowchart, Symbols of flowchart, how to prepare flowchart, Algorithm design, Pseudo code

allSyllabusUnits.title: Fundamentals of C
allSyllabusUnits.topics: History of C, Structure of C program, compilation and execution, Compiler and Interpreter, C tokens, character set, Data Types, Keywords, Identifiers, constants & variables, declaring and assigning value to variable, operators, Input and output function, Type conversion and type casting

allSyllabusUnits.title: Decision statements & looping
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Decision making statements, simple If statement, If-else, nested If- else, else-if ladder, switched statement, goto statement, Looping statements, simple for loop, nested for loop, while & do-while loop

allSyllabusUnits.title: Array, String & Pointer
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Types of arrays, declaration & initialization of 1-D array, operation in array, String- declaration & initialization, string functions, string arrays, Pointer-definition, importance of pointers, declaration & initialization of pointer, accessing the address of a variable through pointers, pointer & array, pointer & string

allSyllabusUnits.title: Function
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition of function, Built-in-function- Math function, console & standard i/o function,, user defined function, recursion

allSyllabusUnits.title: Structure & Union
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition of structure, need of structure, declaration of structure, array within structure, structure within structure, structure and union difference

allSyllabusUnits.title: File management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, file management functions, opening and closing a file, Output operations on files,, error handling during I/O operations, Random Access to file Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Flowchart & Algorithm; Fundamentals of C; Decision statements & looping.

subjects.name: Enviornment Conservation & Disater Management
subjects.objective: Objectives of introducing this subject at first year level in all the branches are:  To sensitize the students to environmental concerns and their impact on society and business  To familiarize the students with strategies for addressing environmental issues  Be better prepared to recover from a major natural catastrophe
course_outcomes: Understand the ecosystem and its terminology and solve various engineering problems by applying ecosystem knowledge to produce eco friendly products
Understand the various types of pollutions and their remedial measures
Understand different renewable energy resources and their applications
Understand the role of an engineer concerning climate change and disaster management

allSyllabusUnits.title: Introduction of Environmental Science
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition of environment, ecosystem, food chain, and food web, he necessity of environmental science, Importance of environment and scope

allSyllabusUnits.title: Types of pollution with their causes, effects and remedial
allSyllabusUnits.topics: measures Air pollution, water pollution, noise pollution, and soil pollution, Global environment problems with their causes, effects & remedies: climate change

allSyllabusUnits.title: Renewable Sources of Energy
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Solar energy: basics of solar energy and its importance, Wind energy: need, limitations and future scope, Recent trends of renewable sources of energy

allSyllabusUnits.title: Disaster Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Concepts and definition of disaster, Disaster management cycle, ole of an engineer in disaster management Rescue techniques during a disaster, Natural disasters: earthquake, cyclone, flood, tsunami, drought, and landslides, Manmade disaster: fire, civil war, technological disasters Total Hours 28

firstHalfUnits.title: Types of pollution with their causes, effects and remedial

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Introduction of Environmental Science; Types of pollution with their causes, effects and remedial; Renewable Sources of Energy.

subjects.name: Integrated Personality Development Course-I
subjects.objective:  This course aims to help a person understand and know his / her purpose in life, get a positive thought pattern, gain confidence, improve behaviour, learn better communication and develop a healthy physique with morality and ethics in its core.  Today youth lack the guidance to face insecurity about their health and career, premature relationships and family breakdown, addictions and substance abuse, negative impact of internet and social media etc. This course includes such topics that will cover all aspects and provide solution to the current challenges through creative and interactive activities.  This course will allow students to enjoy, understand and practice invaluable lessons preparing them for a successful future.
course_outcomes: 1. To provide students with a holistic value-based education that will enable them to be successful in their academic, professional, and social lives.
2. To give the students the tools to develop effective habits, promote personal growth, and improve their well being, stability, and productivity.
3. To allow students to establish a stronger connection with their family through critical thinking and development of qualities such as unity, forgiveness, empathy, and effective communication.
4. To provide students with soft skills that complement their hard skills, making them more marketable when entering the workforce.
5. To enhance awareness of India s glory and global values, and to create considerate citizens who strive for the betterment of their family, college, workforce, and nation.
6. To inspire students to strive for a higher sense of character by learning from role models who have lived principled, disciplined, and value-based lives.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Restructuring Yourself
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students learn how self-improvement enables them to secure a bright future for themselves. They will learn 6 powerful thought- processes that can develop their intellectual, physical, emotional, and spiritual quotients.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Power of Habit
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will undergo a study of how habits work, the habits of successful professionals, and the practical techniques that can be used to develop good habits in their life.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Learning from Legends- Tendulkar & Tata
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn from the inspirational lives of India's two legends, Sachin Tendulkar and Ratan Tata. They will implement these lessons through relatable case studies.

allSyllabusUnits.title: From House to Home Listening & Understanding
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Active listening is an essential part of academic progress and communications. Students will learn to listen with their eyes, ears, mind, and heart.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Welcoming Challenges
allSyllabusUnits.topics: This lecture enables students to revisit the way in which they approach challenges. Through the study of successful figures such as Disney, Lincoln and Bachchan, students will learn to face difficulties through a positive perspective.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Significance of Failures
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Failure is a student¶s daily source of fear, negativity, and depression. Students will be given the constructive skills to understand failure as formative learning experiences.

allSyllabusUnits.title: My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-1
allSyllabusUnits.topics: India¶s ancient Rishis, scholars, and intellectuals have made tremendous contributions to the world, they developed an advanced, sophisticated culture and civilization which began thousands of years ago. Students will learn the importance of studying India¶s glorious past so that they could develop a strong passion and pride for our nation.

allSyllabusUnits.title: My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-2
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Our ancient concepts can be used to seek revolutionary ideas and to generate inspiration. Students will develop a deeper interest in India¶s Glorious Past ± by appreciating the need to read about it, research it, write about it, and share it.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Learning from Legends A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Dr Kalam¶s inspirational life displayed legendary qualities which apply to students (1) Dare to Dream (2) Work Hard (3) Get Good Guidance (4) Humility (5) Use Your Talents for the Benefit of Others

allSyllabusUnits.title: Soft Skills Networking & Leadership
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students are taught the means of building a professional network and developing a leadership attitude.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Soft Skills Project Management
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn the secrets of project management through the Akshardham case study. They will then practice these skills through an activity relevant to student life.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Remaking Yourself Handling Social Media
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn how social media can become addictive and they will imbibe simple methods to take back control.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Facing Failures Power of Faith
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn about the power and necessity of faith in our daily lives.

allSyllabusUnits.title: From House to Home Bonding the Family
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will understand the importance of strong family relationships. They will learn how to overcome the generation gap and connect with their family more.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Selfless Service Seva
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Students will learn that performing seva is beneficial to one¶s health, wellbeing, and happiness. It also benefits and inspires others. Total Hours 30

firstHalfUnits.title: From House to Home Listening & Understanding
My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-1
My India My Pride Glorious Past Part-2

subjects.name: Mathematics-II
subjects.objective: Students are intended to understand the basic concepts and principles of Mathematics such as algebra, mensuration and trigonometry. This knowledge is required to understand and solve Engineering problems. The course will empower students to use proper Mathematical tool to understand Engineering principles and concepts. Main objective of the course is to apply concepts of algebra, mensuration, trigonometry or suitable Mathematical tool to solve given engineering problems.
course_outcomes: Learn concept of Matrix and Determinant and solve the system of linear equations by using matrix.
Solve equations of algebraic expressions using algebraic skills.
Solve the problems using functions.
Solve the problem of function using the concept of Limit.
Find the nth term and Sum of arithmetic and geometric progression.

allSyllabusUnits.title: Determinants and Matrices
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Algebra of Matrices, Determinant of Matrix, Inverse of Matrix up to 3×3 matrix, Solution of Simultaneous Equation (up to 3 variable)

allSyllabusUnits.title: Equations
allSyllabusUnits.topics: System of Linear Equation, Solution of Quadratic Equation, Solution of Cubic Equation

allSyllabusUnits.title: Function
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction of Function, Algebra of Function, Example of Function

allSyllabusUnits.title: Limit of functions
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Definition and some properties of limits, Limit of polynomial and rational functions, Limit of trigonometric function, Limit of exponential function, Limit at infinity

allSyllabusUnits.title: Arithmetic and Geometric Progression
allSyllabusUnits.topics: Introduction, Nth term of A.P, Sum of first N terms of A.P, Nth term of G.P, Sum of first N terms of G.P Total Hours 28

examTypes.syllabusScope: First 50% of the syllabus by ordered units/contact hours: Determinants and Matrices; Equations.
